features.name: Private on-device dictation
features.tagline: Speak into the text field you are already using.
features.what: Gojo’s dictation feature transcribes speech on your Mac and types the result into the active text field.
features.useful: It is useful when writing, replying, or capturing a thought is faster by voice, but you do not want to copy text from a separate transcription app.
details: Runs on-device without an API key or cloud transcription service
Uses explicit local model choices
Designed to type into the text field already in focus
features.caveat: Dictation requires microphone permission and works best when the intended text field is active.

features.name: Media controls
features.tagline: See and control playback without covering your work.
features.what: Gojo puts the current media source and playback controls in the MacBook-notch workspace.
features.useful: It is useful when you need to pause, skip, scrub, shuffle, or check what is playing without bringing a music or browser window forward.
details: Shows the current track in the notch surface
Provides configurable playback controls
Works with the active media source
features.caveat: Available controls depend on the media source currently providing playback information.

features.name: Clipboard history
features.tagline: Find the thing you copied a few minutes ago.
features.what: Gojo keeps recent copied text available in a searchable clipboard history inside the notch workspace.
features.useful: It is useful when you need to recover an earlier copy without interrupting your current task or opening a separate clipboard manager.
details: Search recent copied text
Keeps clipboard access inside the same notch workspace
Skips content marked private by supported password managers
features.caveat: Clipboard history is a convenience feature, not a replacement for a password manager’s security controls.

features.name: Window controls
features.tagline: Preview, focus, organize, and snap windows from the notch.
features.what: Gojo’s window controls help you inspect open windows, bring one forward, and quickly snap a window when your workspace needs a reset.
features.useful: It is useful when you are moving among several documents or apps and want visual window control close to the top of the screen.
details: Preview and focus open windows
Quick window snapping
Uses Accessibility-trusted operations for window actions
features.caveat: Window operations require macOS Accessibility permission; some apps or windows may limit what can be moved or resized.

features.name: File shelf
features.tagline: Set files down before you drag them where they belong.
features.what: Gojo provides a temporary file shelf in the notch so you can stage files while moving between folders, desktops, and apps.
features.useful: It is useful for collecting attachments, rearranging a Finder workflow, or holding a file briefly before dropping it into its destination.
details: Drag files into a temporary notch shelf
Keep staged files available while switching apps
Drag files from the shelf to their destination
features.caveat: The shelf is for temporary staging, not permanent file storage or backup.

features.name: Display comfort controls
features.tagline: Reach Night Shift and display comfort controls from the same workspace.
features.what: Gojo exposes display comfort controls, including Night Shift access, in its compact notch workspace.
features.useful: It is useful when you want to adjust screen warmth as the day changes without hunting through system settings or adding another menu-bar utility.
details: Quick access to Night Shift
Display comfort controls in the notch workspace
Keeps a display adjustment close to other daily utilities
features.caveat: The available display settings and their behavior are governed by macOS and your connected displays.

features.name: Calendar and reminders
features.tagline: Keep the next commitment in view.
features.what: Gojo can place calendar and reminder information among the glanceable tools in the notch workspace.
features.useful: It is useful when you need a quick check of what is next without opening Calendar or losing the context of the app you are working in.
details: Calendar information in the notch workspace
Reminder-related glanceable information
Can be kept out of the way when not needed
features.caveat: Calendar and reminder availability depends on the permissions and accounts configured in macOS.

features.name: Battery status
features.tagline: Check MacBook power at a glance.
features.what: Gojo surfaces MacBook battery status as a compact, glanceable part of the notch experience.
features.useful: It is useful when you want to check charge state, charging status, or low-power context without opening Control Center.
details: Displays MacBook battery status
Shows charging and plugged-in context
Supports low-power-mode state awareness
features.caveat: Battery information reflects the state macOS makes available to Gojo.

features.name: Camera mirror
features.tagline: Check your framing before a call.
features.what: Gojo includes a webcam mirror so you can quickly check the camera view from the notch workspace.
features.useful: It is useful for a fast appearance or framing check before joining a meeting, without opening a full camera application.
details: Quick camera preview
Lives alongside other daily controls
Designed for a brief visual check
features.caveat: Using the camera requires macOS camera permission and may conflict with an app that is already using the camera.

features.name: Shortcuts
features.tagline: Keep your chosen actions close to the rest of your Mac tools.
features.what: Gojo can surface shortcuts as part of the customizable set of tools in the notch workspace.
features.useful: It is useful when a repeatable action belongs next to media, files, windows, and other controls you reach for throughout the day.
details: Part of Gojo’s customizable tool selection
Keeps chosen actions close to the notch workspace
Can be hidden when it does not match your workflow
features.caveat: The exact actions available depend on the shortcuts configured on your Mac.
